recs.title: The Effect of Scripts and Formats on LLM Numeracy
recs.summary: It is shown that LLM accuracy drops substantially when numerical inputs are rendered in underrepresented scripts or formats, despite the underlying mathematical reasoning being identical, and that targeted prompting strategies can greatly narrow this gap.
recs.why: past year · cites 3 in your list

recs.title: Generalizing Numerical Reasoning in Table Data through Operation Sketches and Self-Supervised Learning
recs.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: TaNOS is introduced, a continual pretraining framework comprising three components: header anonymization to reduce lexical memorization, operation sketches that provide minimal structural cues, and self-supervised pretraining that constructs correctness-guaranteed program–question pairs from given tables in a program-first manner that improves the transferability of numerical reasoning.
recs.why: past year · cites 3 in your list

recs.title: Numeracy for Language Models: Evaluating and Improving their Ability to Predict Numbers
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper explores different strategies for modelling numerals with language models, such as memorisation and digit-by-digit composition, and proposes a novel neural architecture that uses a continuous probability density function to model numerals from an open vocabulary.

recs.title: Can neural networks do arithmetic? A survey on the elementary numerical skills of state-of-the-art deep learning models
recs.summary: This survey critically examines the recent literature, concluding that even state-of-the-art architectures and large language models often fall short when probed with relatively simple tasks designed to test basic numerical and arithmetic knowledge.

recs.title: Mining Numbers in Text: A Survey
recs.summary: A quick overview of the history and recent advances of the research of mining such relations between numerals and words found in text data is provided.

recs.title: A Primer for Neural Arithmetic Logic Modules
recs.summary: Focusing on the shortcomings of the NALU, an in-depth analysis is provided to reason about design choices of recent modules, and a benchmark is created which compares all existing arithmetic NALMs.

recs.title: Predicting Numerals in Text Using Nearest Neighbor Language Models
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

recs.title: Masked Measurement Prediction: Learning to Jointly Predict Quantities and Units from Textual Context
recs.summary: A new Generative Masked Measurement (GeMM) model is introduced that jointly learns to predict numbers along with their units and linear probing of traditional pretrained transformer models (RoBERTa) is used to show that they significantly underperform jointly trained number-unit models.

recs.title: Exploring Numeracy in Word Embeddings
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: Inspired by cognitive studies on how humans perceive numbers, an analysis framework is developed to test how well word embeddings capture two essential properties of numbers: magnitude and numeration.

recs.title: Verb Physics: Relative Physical Knowledge of Actions and Objects
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: An approach to infer relative physical knowledge of actions and objects along five dimensions (e.g., size, weight, and strength) from unstructured natural language text is presented.

recs.title: Learning Division with Neural Arithmetic Logic Modules
recs.summary: It is shown that robustly learning division in a systematic manner remains a challenge even at the simplest level of dividing two numbers, and two novel approaches for division are proposed, one of which is the Neural Reciprocal Unit and the NMRU.

recs.title: Numeracy enhances the Literacy of Language Models
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: A significant improvement in MWP for sentences containing numbers is found, that exponent embeddings are the best number encoders, yielding over 2 points jump in prediction accuracy over a BERT baseline, and that these enhanced literacy skills also generalize to contexts without annotated numbers.

recs.title: How to Leverage Digit Embeddings to Represent Numbers?
recs.summary: This paper explores the use of mathematical priors to compute aggregated digit embeddings and explicitly incorporate these aggregates into transformer models and evaluates the effectiveness of incorporating this explicit aggregation.

recs.title: Laying Anchors: Semantically Priming Numerals in Language Modeling
recs.summary: This work introduces strategies to semantically prime numerals in any corpus by generating anchors governed by the distribution of numerals in said corpus, thereby enabling mathematically grounded representations of these numeral tokens in any corpus.

recs.title: The Value of Numbers in Clinical Text Classification
recs.summary: The results showed that even a handful of numerical features can significantly improve text classification performance, and it was concluded that commonly used document representations do not represent numbers in a way that machine learning algorithms can effectively utilize them as features.

recs.title: Exploring the Numerical Reasoning Capabilities of Language Models: A Comprehensive Analysis on Tabular Data
recs.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
recs.summary: A hierarchical taxonomy for numerical reasoning skills with more than ten reasoning types across four levels: representation, number sense, manipulation, and complex reasoning is proposed.

recs.title: Exploring Internal Numeracy in Language Models: A Case Study on ALBERT
recs.summary: These findings illustrate that language models, trained purely to model text, can intuit basic mathematical concepts, opening avenues for NLP applications that intersect with quantitative reasoning.

recs.title: Numerical Correlation in Text
recs.summary: A new task, Numerical Correlation in Text, which requires models to identify the correlation between two numbers in a sentence is proposed and a new dataset is introduced, which contains over 2,000 Wikipedia sentences with two numbers and their correlation labels.

recs.title: Overcoming Barriers to Skill Injection in Language Modeling: Case Study in Arithmetic
recs.summary: This work develops a novel framework that enables language models to be mathematically proficient while retaining their linguistic prowess and offers information-theoretic interventions to overcome the catastrophic forgetting of linguistic skills that occurs while injecting non-linguistic skills into language models.

recs.title: Induced Natural Language Rationales and Interleaved Markup Tokens Enable Extrapolation in Large Language Models
recs.summary: This work demonstrates that large language models can succeed in extrapolation without modifying their architecture or training procedure, and shows how generating step-by-step rationales and introducing marker tokens are both required for effective extrapolation.

recs.title: Improving the Robustness of Neural Multiplication Units with Reversible Stochasticity
recs.summary: It is shown that Neural Multiplication Units (NMUs) are unable to reliably learn tasks as simple as multiplying two inputs when given different training ranges, and stochasticity provides improved robustness with the potential to improve learned representations of upstream networks for numerical and image tasks.

recs.title: NumGPT: Improving Numeracy Ability of Generative Pre-trained Models
affiliations: Department of Computer Science and Engineering, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
recs.summary: The experiment results show that NumGPT outperforms baseline models (e.g., GPT and GPT with DICE) on a range of numerical reasoning tasks such as measurement estimation, number comparison, math word problems, and magnitude classification.

recs.title: Evaluating Numeracy of Language Models as a Natural Language Inference Task
recs.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: This paper proposes a benchmark to evaluate the ability of language models to perform basic numeracy tasks, and frames numeracy as a Natural Language Inference task to assess the models’ ability to understand both numbers and language contexts.

recs.title: Enhancing Knowledge Bases with Quantity Facts
recs.summary: A recall-oriented approach to close the gap in knowledge-base coverage, based on iterative learning for extracting quantity facts, with two novel contributions to boost recall for KB augmentation without sacrificing the quality standards of the knowledge base.

recs.title: Do Language Embeddings capture Scales?
recs.summary: This work identifies contextual information in pre-training and numeracy as two key factors affecting their performance, and shows that a simple method of canonicalizing numbers can have a significant effect on the results.

recs.title: WordNet: A Lexical Database for English
recs.venue: Human Language Technology - The Baltic Perspectiv
recs.summary: WordNet1 provides a more effective combination of traditional lexicographic information and modern computing, and is an online lexical database designed for use under program control.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Children's understanding of counting.
recs.summary: Children learn the meanings of smaller number words before larger ones within their counting range, up to the number three or four, indicating that children learn the cardinal word principle at roughly 3 1/2 years of age.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
affiliations: Facebook AI Research and Tel Aviv University
recs.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: The topmost weight matrix of neural network language models is studied and it is shown that this matrix constitutes a valid word embedding and a new method of regularizing the output embedding is offered.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Variability signatures distinguish verbal from nonverbal counting for both large and small numbers
affiliations: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
recs.summary: The unexpected power-law relation between target value and mean number of presses in nonverbal counting suggests a new hypothesis about the development of the function relating number symbols to mental magnitudes.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: EFFECTIVE TEACHERS OF NUMERACY
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Core systems in human cognition.
recs.summary: Research on human infants, adult nonhuman primates, and children and adults in diverse cultures provides converging evidence for four systems at the foundations of human knowledge.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: Leap-Of-Thought: Teaching Pre-Trained Models to Systematically Reason Over Implicit Knowledge
recs.summary: This work provides a first demonstration that LMs can be trained to reliably perform systematic reasoning combining both implicit, pre-trained knowledge and explicit natural language statements, and demonstrates that models learn to effectively perform inference which involves implicit taxonomic and world knowledge, chaining and counting.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.summary: This paper presents a system for classifying disaster-related tweets, and proposes an annotation schema for identifying relevant tweets as well as the more fine-grained categories they represent, and develop feature-rich classifiers for relevance and fine- grained categorization.

recs.title: From 'F' to 'A' on the N.Y. Regents Science Exams: An Overview of the Aristo Project
recs.summary: Success is reported on the Grade 8 New York Regents Science Exam, where for the first time a system scores more than 90 percent on the exam’s nondiagram, multiple choice (NDMC) questions, demonstrating that modern natural language processing methods can result in mastery on this task.

recs.title: The Biber Cognitive Estimation Test.
recs.summary: The Biber Cognitive Estimation Test (BCET), a 20-item test with five estimation questions in each of four categories: time/duration, quantity, weight, and distance, indicated that the BCET was able to distinguish between demented and intact elderly participants.
recs.why: from Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

recs.title: “Was It Good? It Was Provocative.” Learning the Meaning of Scalar Adjectives
recs.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
recs.summary: It is shown how to ground scalar modifier meaning based on data collected from the Web and that meanings can be learned from Web data and that such meanings can drive pragmatic inference.

recs.title: Grounding Gradable Adjectives through Crowdsourcing
recs.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
recs.summary: A method is proposed for estimating concrete groundings for a set of gradable adjectives that can take a range of magnitudes such as small or slight using crowdsourcing to gather human language intuitions about the impact of each adjective and a linear mixed effects model to this data.
